findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify why a new INDETERMINATE verdict token is preferable to riding a sibling boolean marker (as the existing verdict_obtainable pattern does at completion.py:516) for this fail-closed-but-honest case, or adopt the smaller-blast-radius marker approach.
evidence: completion.py:516 documents the deliberate design choice: verdict_obtainable 'rides ALONGSIDE the {PASS, FAIL} vocabulary rather than adding a third token, so the normalizing fail-safe above, the schema, and every existing consumer's blocking behaviour are unchanged'
schema :16-17 encodes the same marker pattern (verdict_obtainable const false) instead of a new enum token

The plan's own goal is fail-closed (INDETERMINATE still BLOCKS the close), so a sibling marker (e.g. evidence_sufficient=false) riding alongside FAIL would achieve the honesty-of-message goal with strictly smaller blast radius — no schema enum change, no reconcile normalization change, no per-consumer verdict-class handling
findings.finding: The plan chooses to add a third verdict token (INDETERMINATE) touching the schema enum, reconcile normalization, and every consumer, but the codebase's own precedent for exactly this situation (the verdict_obtainable marker) deliberately rides a boolean marker ALONGSIDE the PASS/FAIL vocabulary 'rather than adding a third verdict token' to keep the normalizing fail-safe, schema, and every consumer's blocking behaviour unchanged. The plan does not justify why a new verdict token is superior to the established sibling-marker approach here.
findings.location: Proposed fix / Full consumer graph — Schema bullet ('top-level verdict gains INDETERMINATE')
scenarios: An INDETERMINATE token requires every consumer that switches on verdict (reconcile, close_precheck, sidecar, gate_ops) to learn a third case; a marker leaves the PASS/FAIL switch untouched and adds one branch only where the message is rendered

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in reconcile_verdict that INDETERMINATE is an explicit allowlisted token (all other non-PASS tokens still coerce to FAIL), that the :564 remediation branch emits INDETERMINATE-specific guidance, and how an INDETERMINATE-with-no-findings avoids the verdict_obtainable fault path (:526).
evidence: completion.py:521-522 'verdict = "PASS" if raw == "PASS" else "FAIL"' — INDETERMINATE falls into the else and coerces to FAIL unless the normalization is explicitly widened

completion.py:564 'if verdict == "FAIL": result["remediation"] = COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE else: result.pop("remediation")' — an INDETERMINATE verdict would strip remediation, contradicting 'pass INDETERMINATE through with its own remediation text'

completion.py:526 the verdict_obtainable=False fault-marking keys on 'verdict == FAIL and not items' — the plan never states whether an INDETERMINATE-with-no-findings is legal or how it avoids being marked a verifier fault
findings.finding: The plan says reconcile_verdict must 'pass INDETERMINATE through with its own remediation text; unknown tokens still coerce to FAIL', but does not specify (a) that INDETERMINATE must become an explicit allowlisted token in the normalization at completion.py:521-522 (currently 'PASS' if raw=='PASS' else 'FAIL' — which would coerce INDETERMINATE to FAIL), (b) how the remediation-only-on-FAIL branch (:564) gains an INDETERMINATE branch to carry the distinct remediation, and (c) how an INDETERMINATE with no findings interacts with the verdict_obtainable fault path (:526, which fires 'if verdict == FAIL and not items' and could mis-mark or would be bypassed).
findings.location: Full consumer graph — reconcile_verdict bullet; Scope — src/rebar/llm/completion.py
scenarios: A run banks insufficient_evidence with no positive finding; reconcile must classify it INDETERMINATE with remediation, not FAIL and not a verdict_obtainable fault

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the completion-verifier-finalizer prompt to scope: teach its decision rule and output vocabulary to emit met:null/state:insufficient_evidence (and INDETERMINATE) for a banked insufficient_evidence entry instead of met:false + high-severity finding + FAIL, and remove/qualify the 'verifier prompt changes' out-of-scope exclusion for this finalizer prompt.
evidence: completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-25: 'Set met: true only when the corresponding evidence demonstrates the whole criterion. Missing, incomplete, contradictory, or truncated evidence is not enough and must be met: false.'
completion_verifier_finalizer.md:26: 'Include one high-severity finding for every criterion with met: false.'
completion_verifier_finalizer.md:27-28: 'Return PASS only when every expected criterion is demonstrably met; otherwise return FAIL.'

Prompt front-matter (line 6) 'outputs: completion_verdict' — it emits the very schema the plan widens, but no state=insufficient_evidence / INDETERMINATE interpretation is defined for the emitter (T8(a) undefined referenced vocabulary; T8(b) decision rule not co-located with the schema it emits).

The plan feeds insufficient_evidence into this prompt via _run_finalizer's banked_evidence payload (completion_recovery.py:738-746, :741 'met': bool(entry...)) but 'Out of scope' explicitly excludes 'verifier prompt changes'.
findings.finding: The completion-verifier-finalizer prompt is a live LLM surface that emits the widened completion_verdict schema and consumes the banked_evidence payload the plan modifies, yet the plan updates neither the prompt's decision rule nor its verdict vocabulary — the prompt still instructs the model to collapse insufficient evidence into met:false + a high-severity finding + FAIL, re-introducing the fixed defect at the LLM seam on the primary finalization path.
findings.location: Scope: 'completion_recovery.py — _run_finalizer ... renders the sentinel faithfully (:741)' and 'Out of scope: verifier prompt changes'; prompt src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier_finalizer.md
scenarios: A search-exhausted criterion banks insufficient_evidence; the LLM finalizer runs (the common finalization path), reads the banked_evidence entry, follows its prompt text, and emits met:false + a high-severity finding + FAIL — the exact false-FAIL the plan set out to eliminate, now originating in the LLM turn and passed through by merge_finalizer_with_bank.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise completion_verifier_finalizer.md lines 23-28 to distinguish 'evidence refutes the criterion' (met:false, finding, contributes to FAIL) from 'the banked record is insufficient_evidence / search-exhausted' (emit the tri-state sentinel / state, no fabricated finding, contributes to INDETERMINATE) and define the INDETERMINATE verdict token there, mirroring the schema and reconcile_verdict changes; narrow the Out-of-scope exclusion accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `successor_instructions` (completion_banking.py:149) to the consumer graph and render `insufficient_evidence` bank entries as not-yet-determined (re-verify) rather than `met=False (do NOT re-verify)`; re-derive the banked-`met` consumer inventory via find_referencing_symbols on the bank read path plus a grep for `get("met")`/`["met"]`.
evidence: Plan: `_run_finalizer (completion_recovery.py:741): bool(entry.get('met')) collapses the sentinel to false before the LLM finalizer sees it — render insufficient_evidence faithfully`
Omitted site: completion_banking.py:149 `f"- {cid}: met={bool(entry.get('met'))} (already verified — do NOT re-verify)"` inside successor_instructions
successor_instructions consumes bank.all() at completion_recovery.py:667-669, so an exhaustion-banked insufficient_evidence entry from a prior batch flows here
findings.finding: The consumer graph for the banked per-criterion `met` value omits `successor_instructions` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:149), a banked-evidence renderer that coerces the tri-state to bool. It receives `bank.all()` (completion_recovery.py:667-669) and renders `met={bool(entry.get('met'))}`; for an `insufficient_evidence` entry (`met=None`) this collapses to `met=False` and prints '(already verified — do NOT re-verify)', telling the next successor batch the criterion was refuted and locking it out of re-verification. This is the same class of bool-coercion the plan explicitly patches at `_run_finalizer` (:741) but is not listed.
findings.location: Full consumer graph section / Scope; plan lists `_run_finalizer` (completion_recovery.py:741) as the banked-evidence renderer but omits `successor_instructions`.
scenarios: completion_banking.py:149 successor_instructions: an insufficient_evidence bank entry (met=None) renders as `met=False (already verified — do NOT re-verify)`, telling the next batch the criterion is refuted and suppressing the re-verification the tri-state was meant to enable — silently defeating the plan's premise.
findings.suggested_fix: In successor_instructions, branch on the entry's tri-state: for an insufficient_evidence entry emit a 'search exhausted — re-verify' line (and keep it in the remainder set) instead of 'met=False … do NOT re-verify'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the invariant relating met and state at write time (e.g. state is authoritative; met=None iff state=insufficient_evidence; met∈{true,false} iff state∈{met,unmet}) and define precisely what 'untyped record' _validate_coverage rejects.

'_validate_coverage accepts the tri-state and still rejects untyped records' — 'untyped' is undefined given both a nullable met and a state field exist
findings.finding: The write path persists 'met: bool | None + explicit state', and the schema state enum is met/unmet/insufficient_evidence, but the plan does not pin the exact correspondence between the nullable bool and the state string at write time (e.g. does met=true always imply state='met'? is met=None the sole carrier of insufficient_evidence, or must state be present?). A round-trip (harvest, sidecar, _validate_coverage 'still rejecting untyped records') depends on which field is authoritative when they could disagree.
findings.location: Proposed fix: 'CriterionBank.upsert … widen to persist the tri-state (met: bool | None + explicit state)'
scenarios: A re-harvested entry with met=false but state absent, or met=None with state='met' — the executor must guess which field wins and what 'untyped' rejects.

The plan should reconcile these two third-state mechanisms so they remain intentionally distinct rather than accidentally divergent or duplicative.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the new INDETERMINATE verdict token against (a) the established inconclusive/three-valued verdict pattern (e.g. NUnit Assert.Inconclusive) and (b) the repo's existing `verdict_obtainable` additive marker (schema.json:14-18) — state why a third token flowing through the whole consumer graph is preferred over extending the marker approach, or adopt the marker approach.
evidence: Plan: 'top-level `verdict` (:10-12) gains `INDETERMINATE`, emitted when no criterion is `unmet` but ≥1 is `insufficient_evidence`'

In-repo precedent (schema.json:16): `verdict_obtainable` 'rides ALONGSIDE the PASS/FAIL vocabulary rather than adding a third verdict token, so `verdict` stays `FAIL` and every existing consumer still blocks fail-closed' — the opposite of the plan's approach, unacknowledged.

Retrieved prior art (NUnit docs, docs.nunit.org): Assert.Inconclusive 'indicates that the test could not be completed with the data available... another run with different data might run to completion' — an established inconclusive-verdict pattern the plan never cites.
The plan's Context/Proposed fix/Scope sections contain no prior-art or alternative-design discussion.
findings.finding: The plan adds a novel third-verdict-token architecture (INDETERMINATE + insufficient_evidence threaded through the whole consumer graph) without considering established prior art for inconclusive/three-valued verdicts, nor the repo's own existing `verdict_obtainable` marker which deliberately handles 'verifier could not affirmatively determine' WITHOUT a third token.
findings.location: Proposed fix / 'Full consumer graph' — top-level `verdict` gains `INDETERMINATE`; completion_verdict.schema.json:10-18
scenarios: Reviewer/author later asks why a new verdict token was preferred over extending the existing `verdict_obtainable` fault-marker (which already blocks fail-closed and rides alongside FAIL), and the plan offers no rationale.
The tri-state token propagation to reconcile_verdict/close_precheck/rendering seams turns out to duplicate machinery `verdict_obtainable` already provides for the fail-closed path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art / design rationale' note: cite the established inconclusive-verdict pattern, then explicitly contrast the two in-repo options — (1) a full third verdict token (INDETERMINATE, this plan) vs (2) an additive `insufficient_evidence`-style marker riding alongside FAIL like `verdict_obtainable` does — and record why option (1) is chosen (e.g. that consumers must render/report it distinctly, not merely fail-closed). If the fail-closed behavior is identical to `verdict_obtainable`, justify not reusing that mechanism.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify precedence between the new INDETERMINATE verdict token and the existing verdict_obtainable=false fault marker (which dominates when both apply), and update the schema's verdict_obtainable design note that asserts 'no third verdict token' is added on the completion path.
evidence: completion_verdict.schema.json:16: verdict_obtainable 'rides ALONGSIDE the PASS/FAIL vocabulary rather than adding a third verdict token, so verdict stays FAIL and every existing consumer still blocks fail-closed.'

The plan now DOES add a third verdict token (INDETERMINATE) to the same verdict field but never addresses this prior design decision or how INDETERMINATE coexists with verdict_obtainable=false (both are non-PASS, non-FAIL semantics on the completion path).

reconcile_verdict (completion.py:508-519) sets verdict_obtainable=False on a fault while keeping verdict='FAIL'; the plan's INDETERMINATE path and this fault path are both reached from the same non-PASS handling but their precedence is unspecified.
findings.finding: The plan adds INDETERMINATE as a third token to the completion verdict field, but the schema's existing verdict_obtainable marker was deliberately designed to avoid a third completion verdict token; the plan does not reconcile the two mechanisms nor define the combined state (a run that is both a verifier-fault and has insufficient_evidence).
findings.location: Plan 'Full consumer graph' → Schema bullet ('top-level verdict (:10-12) gains INDETERMINATE'); completion_verdict.schema.json:14-17 (verdict_obtainable), :10-12 (verdict)
scenarios: A verifier fault (no obtainable verdict) co-occurs with insufficient_evidence criteria: it is undefined whether the run reports verdict='FAIL' + verdict_obtainable=false (existing retryable-fault semantics, exit 11) or verdict='INDETERMINATE' (new semantics), so close_precheck's _raise_on_verifier_fault vs INDETERMINATE-remediation branch is ambiguous.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the back-out behavior for records already persisted in the new tri-state format (e.g. a down-migration coercing met=null/insufficient_evidence -> met:false, or a documented assertion that reverting is safe because banks are ephemeral per-run).
evidence: 'absent state + bool met stays valid for existing records' establishes forward-compat only
ABSENCE: no statement of how records written in the new tri-state format behave if the change is rolled back — the reverse migration direction is unaddressed
findings.finding: The plan changes the completion_verdict schema (met bool -> boolean|null + state enum) and adds an INDETERMINATE verdict token, and explicitly preserves FORWARD compatibility (old all-bool records still validate) but states no BACK-OUT path for records written in the NEW tri-state format. If this change is reverted after tickets have banked met=null / state=insufficient_evidence entries or an INDETERMINATE verdict, pre-change strict-bool validators (_validate_coverage hard-raise, schema :31 strict bool) would reject those persisted records.
findings.location: Scope: completion_verdict.schema.json — 'criteria[].met boolean|null + state enum + INDETERMINATE verdict token (backward compatible)'
scenarios: Change lands, tickets bank insufficient_evidence entries, then a regression forces revert — old strict-bool _validate_coverage/schema reject the met=null records and error on read.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Out-of-scope/rollback note: banks are per-run ephemeral so no persisted tri-state survives a revert; OR specify a down-conversion mapping (insufficient_evidence -> met:false) applied on read by the reverted code.
